newsitem.title: JORDAN: Iraq-bound food cargo arrives at Aqaba port.
newsitem.headline: Iraq-bound food cargo arrives at Aqaba port.

text.p: The first Iraq-bound shipment of food to be sent through Jordan under an oil-for-food deal with the United Nations has docked at the kingdom's Red Sea port of Aqaba, shippers said on Friday.
The vessel carrying 52,500 tonnes of French wheat, sold by supplier Glencore, arrived early on Friday, they said.
Shippers said another 50,000 tonnes shipment of French wheat sold to Iraq from the same supplier was due early next month via Aqaba.
Another 150,000 tonnes of French wheat purchased by Iraq from L. Dreyfus are expected to be discharged in Aqaba in three shipments over the coming few months, shippers said.
Activity at Aqaba port was badly hit since most Iraqi shipments were halted with the imposition of a U.N. embargo on Iraq after it invaded Kuwait in 1990.
So far most of Baghdad's grains imports under the oil-for-food deal are being delivered to Um Qasr, Iraq's sole sea outlet.
Aqaba, built as a regional port, is a key unloading port under the U.N. deal, and officials and shippers hope at least 20 percent of the purchases will be handled through it.
